title: Time Jump — 08:50, Draft Control-Area Map In

fields.narration: It is now 08:50 on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, one hour after the presumptive result. The EOC is open at Level 2 in the Public Safety Building Training Room. At 08:44 the Board of Animal Health planning section emailed DRAFT v1 of the control-area map. It is marked 'NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE'. The legend reads: 'Infected zone 3 km and buffer zone 7 km (together the 10 km control area); surveillance zone at least 10 km wide beyond. Federal HPAI plan planning values. The Minnesota plan governs, and Board epidemiology may widen any zone.' On the draft, the Prairie Gold feed mill in Larkin sits inside the buffer zone, about 6 km from IP-1. The Dunmore processing plant is outside the control area. On the grower group text, people are calling the mill 'shut down'. The Annex K clocks are running. The first four of the 11 checkpoints are due at 10:50, the quarantine order at 11:50, and the control area at 15:50. The Sheriff's day shift has six deputies, and two of them are tied up on a rollover crash on the State Highway. That leaves enough people for three checkpoint sites, not four.
worldState: Clock: 08:50, Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Still 29°F to low 30s, clear, light northwest wind.
The EOC is open at Level 2, Public Safety Building Training Room, Larkin.

The Board's DRAFT v1 control-area map (received 08:44) is marked NOT FOR PUBLIC RELEASE. Its zone sizes are federal planning values: the Minnesota plan governs, and Board epidemiology may widen any zone.
The Prairie Gold feed mill in Larkin is inside the draft buffer zone, about 6 km from IP-1. Nobody has ordered it closed. The grower group text says it is 'shut down'.
The Dunmore processing plant (410 employees) is outside the draft control area.
National reference laboratory confirmation is still pending. The Board is acting on the presumptive result.

Annex K clocks from the 07:50 presumptive result: first four checkpoints by 10:50; quarantine order by 11:50; control area and all 11 checkpoints by 15:50; public producer and consumer notice by 19:50; every IP-1 barn depopulated by 07:50 Wednesday.

The four primary checkpoint sites are County Roads 12, 14 and 21 and State Highway 9. Each one needs two deputies or reserve officers, a county highway worker, a sign set, a handwash station and a C&D sprayer.

The Sheriff has four deputies available, enough for three sites. Two deputies are working a rollover crash on the State Highway. Mutual aid relief from the Pell and Ritter county sheriffs is planned only after hour 8.
The Board's 09:30 deadline to confirm IP-1's address, barn count and access roads is still open.
CR 31 is closed between 190th and 200th Street from 09:00 for the culvert replacement.
fields.facilitatorNote: Watch for: the EMD logs DRAFT v1 as the Board's product and keeps its distances out of public channels (CCACMP 10). OPS and the Sheriff give the three staffed sites to the roads that carry turkey, feed, shavings and rendering traffic, treat the fourth site as a coming miss of the 10:50 clock, and tell the Board now instead of at 10:50 (Annex K 4.2–4.3). PROD asks the permit coordinator about a mill movement permit and does not let the mill be treated as closed. If no one notices that the unguarded 230th Street field lane may need coverage, prompt with: 'Which roads actually carry the trucks?'
fields.scenarioTitle: Flyway — HPAI Control Area, Checkpoints & Depopulation

instructorNote: This card opens Phase 2. It tests whether the players treat the draft map as the Board's unreleased product, rank the three staffable checkpoints by truck traffic and report the fourth-site shortfall to the Board early, and steer the mill toward a permit rather than a shutdown. Watch for anyone quoting the 3/7/10 km figures to growers or the public.
